title: Customer feedback: causal flows and prioritized feature asks (May 2027)
content:
Purpose and scope

This note synthesizes raw CS field feedback gathered Apr 15 – May 2, 2027 and maps causal chains from customer reports to concrete feature asks and low/medium/high effort fixes. The goal is to give eng/product clear hypotheses to validate, measurable signals to watch, and quick experiments we can ship in 2–6 weeks.

High-level signal summary
- Predominant themes: unexpected latency spikes under burst traffic, model fallbacks producing lower-quality outputs during autoscale, and confusion about cost/quantization tradeoffs for Dedicated and Private modes.
- Anchor metric: customers calling out tail latency > 800 ms (token generation) for 95th percentile under burst windows of 5–15s.
- Secondary signals: increase in support threads labeled "quality regression" after recent routing policy change; multiple customers requesting per-request QoS routing override.

Method: causal-flow approach
- Step 1: cluster raw quotes into symptom buckets.
- Step 2: for each bucket, trace the most plausible upstream cause(s) using engineering knowledge and recent infra changes.
- Step 3: propose feature asks or tactical mitigations and map to signal tests.

Symptom bucket A: 'intermittent high tail latency'
Representative quotes
- "Some requests are fine but every few minutes we get 2s+ responses, which kills our UX."
- "We see big latency when we hit concurrent requests after a lull."

Causal hypotheses
1) routing to lower-cost model variant during capacity pressure causes cold-starts or increased queueing.
  - Evidence: correlates with autoscale events in prod logs (Eng ticket ENG-1304).
2) batching heuristics timed poorly for bursty arrival patterns causing queue buildups then big simultaneous dispatches.
  - Evidence: customer telemetry shows short bursts of many small requests; current continuous-batching window tuned for steady traffic.
3) KV cache warmup after model variant swap leads to per-request spikes for early tokens.
  - Evidence: customers report spikes mostly at the start of sessions.

Proposed asks and quick wins
- Quick win Q1 (2 weeks): expose per-route 'burst-mode' hint (boolean) so caller can opt into reduced-batching/priority scheduling for low-latency slices. Minimal console and API flag, server-side hook to bypass batching heuristics for flagged routes. Signal to watch: 95th percentile latency on flagged routes.
- Medium work M1 (6–8 weeks): routing policy toggle to prefer stable model variants for SLO-critical routes and avoid cold-start fallbacks. Includes console UI and simple policy DSL. Signal: fallback frequency vs SLO violations.
- Medium work M2 (6–10 weeks): KV cache prewarm API for Dedicated customers to warm caches on deploy/variant switch. Signal: early-session latency reduction.

Symptom bucket B: 'sudden drop in output quality after autoscale/fallback'
Representative quotes
- "When load is high, we get a different voice/tone and answers go off. It's clearly a different model variant."

Causal hypotheses
1) fallback to smaller quantized model variants without downstream prompt adjustments.
2) lack of quality metadata surfaced to customer when model switch happens.

Proposed asks
- Quick win Q2 (1–3 weeks): add an explicit 'model-variant-change' header in API responses and console logs to make it visible to customers and CS. Low dev cost. Signal: decrease in 'unknown-regression' support threads; customers can self-triage.
- Medium work M3 (8–12 weeks): introduce model-variant guardrails: automated safety nets to run prompts through a lightweight quality-checker before returning when variant changed. Could be an optional checkbox per-route. Signal: regression rate for flagged prompts.

Symptom bucket C: 'unclear cost/quantization guidance for Dedicated and Private'
Quotes
- "We want concrete rules of thumb: when should we quantize, and what quality delta to expect?"

Causal hypotheses
- Documentation and tooling gap: Optimize recommendations are too generic; customers need workload-specific estimates.

Proposed asks
- Quick win Q3 (2 weeks): produce 3 short guidance docs + per-route examples (QPS patterns: chat, completion, embeddings) mapping quantization profiles to observed quality delta and cost delta. Work with Applied ML to run benchmarks.
- Medium work M4 (6 weeks): add a 'simulate-cost-quality' button in Console where customers can upload a small representative prompt set and get an estimated cost vs quality tradeoff matrix (uses sandbox estimate; no real traffic). Signal: reduction in pre-sales calls asking about quantization.

Traffic archetypes mapping (why this matters)
- 'Chat-first' customers: many small messages, latency-sensitive, prefer lower batching and model stability. Priority: Q1, Q2.
- 'Batch-embeddings' customers: high throughput, can tolerate higher batching; prefer cost-optimized variants. Priority: M4, doc guidance.
- 'Regulated/private' customers: require deterministic model pinning and explicit change notifications. Priority: M1, Q2.

Prioritization matrix (CS view)
- Impact vs Effort ranking (approx):
  1) Q2 model-variant header: high impact, low effort -> ship immediately.
  2) Q1 burst-mode hint: high impact for latency-sensitive customers, low engineering risk -> ship as opt-in.
  3) Q3 guidance docs: medium impact, low effort -> couple with Q1 rollout.
  4) M1 routing policy toggle: high impact, medium effort -> schedule R&D sprint.
  5) M4 simulate-cost-quality console feature: medium impact, medium effort -> product backlog.

Signal definitions and how to measure success
- Latency SLO breach: 95th token-gen latency > 800ms over rolling 1h window.
- Fallback frequency: percent of requests that served a variant different from pinned variant within a tenant's traffic.
- Regression chatter: count of support threads tagged 'quality-regression' per week.
- Prewarm effectiveness: delta in first-10-token latency pre/post prewarm API.

Open questions and unknowns
- How intrusive will burst-mode be for overall cluster throughput? Potential tradeoff with cost; need SRE input.
- Guardrail false positives for pre-check quality gates could add latency; applied-ml should estimate ROC for the lightweight checker.
- Billing surface for simulate-cost-quality: is sandbox estimation billable or free? Needs finance guidance.

Next steps and owners
- Ship Q2 header: owner Liam Chen, ETA May 18, 2027. (low-risk API change and CS communication).
- Implement Q1 hint prototype: owner Marco Ruiz, coordinate with SRE to test effect on batching; prototype by May 30.
- Prep Q3 guidance docs and benchmark runs: owner Anika Patel + Applied ML (Sofia Alvarez) draft by May 24.
- Convene cross-functional triage sync: CS, Eng-serving-runtime, Applied-ML, SRE on May 14 to align signals and measurement.

Appendix: raw quote snippets (redacted)
- "We started getting worse responses after midnight scale-up. It felt like someone swapped the model."
- "If we could pin our route to 'low-latency mode' we'd probably accept higher spend."
- "Docs don't say what happens to embeddings quality when you switch to 4-bit quantized model. We need numbers."

Notes to reviewers
- This is a field-first synthesis intended to be actionable; please flag any engineering constraints early. If you disagree with priority ordering, mark reasons in inline comments and we'll re-run the matrix.

Unresolved: scheduling for routing-policy sprint pending eng capacity confirmation.

End of note.
